clarity.justification: The proposal clearly varies confounder availability, probes internal representations, and compares them with observational and causal ground truth, with highly decidable criteria such as “Index >= 10 points,” “flip-toward-correct fraction >= 0.8,” and explicit refutation thresholds. However, the inference that these tests distinguish an adjustment mechanism from ordinary conditioning is not secure: contrary to “an association-only model responds identically,” a predictive conditioner can change when Z is supplied and can recover a sign reversal because backdoor adjustment itself uses conditional distributions. Experiment 3 also contains a logical ambiguity because it varies only “Z-to-X and Z-to-Y coupling” while expecting the “true interventional effect” to cross zero, although changing confounding strength alone normally changes the observational association rather than the causal X-to-Y effect.

feasibility.justification: The hardest step is measuring and intervening on the architecture-specific quantity described as the “predicted X->Y effect shift toward the do-calculus answer under adjustment steering”; activation extraction and matched-norm steering are standard operations, but the exact TabPFN activation aggregation and prediction-to-effect mapping remain under-specified. TabPFN exists, and linear probes, CKA, bootstrap evaluation, synthetic SCM generation, and activation interventions have standard tooling support, although the “general tabular baseline” and “semi-realistic tables” are not concretely identified. Resources are usefully quantified through “3,000 synthetic datasets,” “5-fold CV,” “5 seeds,” “20 matched-norm random directions,” and a “~25M parameters” model. The refuting branch is runnable because the design includes shuffled-confounder, non-confounding-column, random-direction, observational-direction, confounder-free, and explicit lower-bracket controls.
